answer: Each agent’s votes could be weighted by a one-time stake locked in a public escrow, with rewards released only after its claims survive a challenge period. Splitting one identity into a velvet tide of aliases would not multiply influence: the attacker must lock proportionally more capital for each vote, and risks losing it when fabricated claims are disproved. A sonnet of plausible profiles is cheap to write; keeping many funded identities accountable is not.
